lead: Test of the 0.8.39 CI build (run 42485251399). risk.py: class C on all three systems, so from the core list the automated runs (hil.sh passed on Linux already: cold start, reopen twice, export, broker killed) and sleep on the Mac. The round's own items come from today: the delay now follows the buffer and uses the original's margin (76 ms instead of 82.7 ms at 64 samples / 48 kHz), notes played on a keyboard skip the delay (live-notes, on by default, about 22 ms), the cut-note fix, the welcome / What's New pages, the manuals in the ? menu, and the start-page order. Our Virus has no keys: in Live the computer keyboard counts as played notes. Mark each item and add a note where something looks different; Claude reads the marks from this page.
rules: Order: Linux first (the Virus is there), then the Mac, then the Windows VM. Close the DAW before the Virus moves.
Never power-cycle the Virus while it is attached to the VM.
Use a disposable project. Nothing in this round stores to the Virus.
No game or other heavy program running during the timing items: it changes the results (seen today).

sections.title: Linux
sections.where: This PC, REAPER, the 0.8.39 CI build (installed by Claude: plug-in 0a4d7357, broker 92f83998)
prep: Nothing to install. Close any game. The Virus is on Linux.

items.title: Small buffers play cleanly and on time
steps: In a terminal: pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.force-quantum 64, then start REAPER with a project that has the plug-in and a clip of 16ths.
Play 30 s. Then the same with clock.force-quantum 32.
Back to normal afterwards: pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.force-quantum 0.
items.expect: No crackle, no dropouts, notes in time with the click. The plug-in's delay in REAPER's performance meter is smaller at 64 and 32 than at 256 (it follows the buffer now).

items.title: The first note after Play
steps: Same project at a normal buffer. Press Play from bar 1 five times, stopping after two bars each time.
Listen to the first note of each start.
items.expect: The first note sounds with the others, not late or missing (simulator S068 predicted a late first note with hosts that send blocks in bursts).

items.title: Reopening a project gives no click
steps: With REAPER open and the project playing, close the project (not REAPER) and open it again within 20 s, so the broker keeps running.
Do it three times, listening at the moment the plug-in starts.
items.expect: No click or pop when the plug-in starts (simulator S078 saw two stray samples at start when the broker kept running).

items.title: Welcome, What's New, manuals and setup tips
steps: Claude moves info-page.state and setup-tips.seen aside first. Open the plug-in in REAPER.
Watch the order: Starting up (and Syncing if banks are read), then What's New, then the setup tips.
Open ? and click a manual.
items.expect: One page after the other, never over the start pages; OK and Don't Show Again work; the manual opens in the PDF viewer.

items.title: No silent start at 44.1 kHz (Claude runs it)
steps: Claude starts 20 sessions at 44.1 kHz with nativehost and a capture, as in E464/E469.
items.expect: Every session plays. If the Virus blocks MIDI during the start (cancelled writes in the capture), the session still plays after it: that proves the stall fix (E469).

sections.title: macOS
sections.where: MacBook Air M3, Ableton Live 12 and Logic Pro, the 0.8.39 CI build (you install the package; Claude pushed it)
prep: Quit the DAW, then double-click Install test build.command in ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.39-mac, or paste: sudo installer -pkg "$HOME/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.39-mac/TI Revive.pkg" -target /
Move the Virus' USB cable to the Mac and switch it on if needed. Claude checks the installed version with pkgutil before trusting a result.
Optional: run hil-mac.command from the package for the automated core items (cold start, reopen, export).

items.title: Played notes are fast, clips stay exact (Live)
steps: Ableton Live 12, the plug-in on a MIDI track with a clip of 16ths. Turn on Live's computer MIDI keyboard.
Play notes on the computer keyboard while stopped, then while the clip runs.
Play the same key as a clip note right after that clip note ends, a few times.
items.expect: Played notes feel immediate (about 22 ms), the clip stays in time, no hanging notes, and a played note is never cut off by the clip's own note of that key.

items.title: Small buffers in Live and Logic
steps: Live: Settings, Audio, buffer 64, play the clip 30 s; then 32 if the Mac offers it.
Logic: I/O buffer 64, Process Buffer Range Small, play a region 30 s.
items.expect: No crackle or dropouts, notes in time. Logic plays as before (its Audio Unit marks no notes as played, so no live path there).

items.title: What's New, manuals and setup tips on the Mac
steps: Open the plug-in in Live. Watch the pages after the start, then open ? and click a manual.
items.expect: What's New shows once after the start pages, then the setup tips; the manual opens in Preview (from /Library/Documentation/Access Music/Virus TI/Manuals).

sections.title: Windows (VM)
sections.where: win11 VM, Ableton Live, the 0.8.39 CI build (installed by Claude, setup.exe /quiet, exit 0)
prep: Claude passes the Virus through to the VM and can run hil-win for the automated core items.

items.title: The plug-in starts and plays; What's New and the manuals
steps: Open the plug-in in Ableton Live in the VM, play a clip.
Watch the pages after the start, then open ? and look at the manual entries.
items.expect: It plays as before; What's New shows after the start pages; the manuals are listed if the Access software is installed in the VM, and open in the PDF viewer.

items.title: Heavy project with the ORIGINAL Virus Control (win10ref)
steps: win10ref, Ableton Live 11, the original Virus Control 5.1.7 (not TI Revive). Claude passes the Virus through and copies the three MIDI files to the VM's Desktop (folder heavy-project).
One track with Virus Control in Multi mode: part 1 Main LD, part 2 Hrd LD 1, part 3 Super Saw. Three MIDI tracks with the looped clips (150 BPM), MIDI To the Virus track on channels 1, 2 and 3.
Run 1: parts on Out 1, Out 2, Out 3 as on the Mac. Play all three 30 s, then two at a time.
Run 2: all parts on Out 1 L/R. Play all three 30 s and listen on the Virus' headphones too.
Run 3, the part swap: move Super Saw to part 2 (or 4) and Hrd LD 1 to part 3, the clips' MIDI channels with them. Play all three 30 s.
items.expect: Note in each run whether notes go missing and in which part. If the original loses the same notes, it is the Virus' own limit (E376's load governor); if the swap changes which notes go missing, the load per DSP is the cause (simulator: parts 1 and 3 share a DSP). VM USB timing is not exact (E288): crackle here proves little, missing notes do.
